text:
Municipal bond interest is free of federal income tax. But when the IRS tests whether your Social Security is taxable, that interest is counted.

• IRS Publication 915: half your benefits + all your other income, including tax-exempt interest
• Our 2026 example: a married couple, both 65+, with $48,000 of Social Security and a $40,000 pension
• Add $10,000 of muni interest and $8,500 more of their benefits becomes taxable
• Their federal tax rises about $850

Hold muni bonds? Count that interest when you check your combined income.

Full video: 401(k), Social Security or Pension: How Claiming Order Affects Tax

Retire at 58 and you're seven years short of Medicare. A popular plan says build five bridges while you work. We price the crossing for an invented couple (Rob and Julie, both 50), and we correct its Roth-conversion rate. Under the 2027 cliff the 22% bracket can't happen, and the real price is 22–31¢ per dollar.

THE SEVEN-YEAR BRIDGE (58 → 65)
Load limit: floor $29,863 · their limit $80,000 · cliff $86,560
1 Cash: one year of spending, $84,000
2 Brokerage: worked backwards, $21,191 a year
3 HSA: $106,028 at 58; bronze plans qualify
4 The 55 door: no 10%, but 20% withheld
5 Conversions: 24.7¢ on the dollar
Seven years: $152,096 of credits kept, $28,776 of federal tax.
